analysis: What changed vs the 5:00 AM brief: October PPI is now in — headline +0.3% MoM vs +0.4% expected, but +6.5% YoY, the highest annual rate since November 2022; core +0.3% matched estimates. Futures firmed after the print (S&P E-mini to ~7,666, +0.31% in the first minutes). The Microsoft drag eased: MSFT is now -1.37% premarket vs -2.6% at 5 AM, and Microsoft's 9:03 AM update reports 'early signs of stabilization' with capacity still not back to normal. Nvidia's bounce held at about +1.8%, and the congressional calendar is now concrete — House closed-door interviews Dec 1-2, Senate Banking Dec 3 (Huang) and Dec 10 (Lutnick, who has agreed to appear voluntarily), with subpoenas threatened. Modine's premium held at about +30% with still no confirmation from either company. Cisco faded about -3% despite a beat and raised outlook, on margins. Bitcoin slipped below $70K (-4.76%). Signal vs noise: PPI's monthly cooling is real relief for the tape, but the 6.5% YoY print and the ex-food/energy/trade measure at +0.5% keep the December-hike story alive — Waller had said a half-point hike should be considered if October core came in at 0.3% or more, and it came in at exactly 0.3%. The Nvidia testimony dates and the Microsoft recovery are the live wires into the open; the Modine and oil premiums still rest on unconfirmed claims.

headlines.headline: October PPI rose 0.3% MoM vs +0.4% expected (September revised up to +1.4%), but +6.5% YoY — the largest annual gain since November 2022. Core PPI +0.3% MoM matched estimates (+5.0% YoY); the ex-food/energy/trade measure rose 0.5%. S&P futures firmed to ~7,666 (+0.31%) in the first minutes after the 8:30 AM ET print.
headlines.why_it_matters: A cooler monthly headline is relief for the tape, but the 6.5% YoY print keeps the December-hike story alive — and with October core at exactly 0.3%, the half-point-hike discussion Waller floated stays on the table.

headlines.headline: Congress set dates for the Nvidia probe: Senate Banking asked Huang to testify Dec 3 and Commerce Secretary Lutnick Dec 10, with subpoenas threatened; three House committees want closed-door interviews Dec 1 (Huang) and Dec 2 (Nvidia counsel Tim Teter). Lutnick has agreed to appear voluntarily, per NBC. NVDA is +1.83% premarket at $169.23, holding its bounce after Thursday's -4.34% close at $166.19.
headlines.why_it_matters: Firm testimony dates turn a governance scandal into a scheduled Washington event — the bounce is relief that the timeline is now known, not resolution of the export-control questions.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's 365 outage is into day two: its 9:03 AM update reports 'early signs of stabilization' but capacity is not yet back to normal, and it extended the email timeout window to 48 hours. MSFT is -1.37% premarket at $515.84, improved from -2.6% at 5 AM. Downdetector logged 120,000+ Outlook problem reports at peak across 74 countries; Microsoft says it is not a cyberattack and no root cause is confirmed.
headlines.why_it_matters: Stabilization is not recovery — a second day without a confirmed root cause keeps the reliability question open, though the stock's premarket drag is easing as service partially returns.

headlines.headline: Modine is +30.3% premarket at $138.25 (vs Thursday's $106.10 close) on the Bloomberg report that Samsung is in talks to acquire the data-center cooling maker. No price disclosed, no decision made, and neither company has confirmed anything.
headlines.why_it_matters: The cooling-layer bid is a sentiment tailwind for AI infrastructure names — but with no confirmation, the premium is fragile. Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Cerebras is +16-18% premarket after a Q3 beat and raised 2026 outlook, with cloud revenue up 272% and market-mover roundups newly naming Microsoft as a cloud customer.
headlines.why_it_matters: A Microsoft customer win would validate Cerebras as a real second source in AI compute — but the customer detail comes from market-mover roundups, not a company release, so treat it as unconfirmed until Cerebras or Microsoft says it.

headlines.headline: Cisco is down about -3% premarket despite beating estimates and raising its outlook, with margins in focus. AAPL is +0.36% premarket at $356.15.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat-and-raise that still sells off on margins is a reminder this earnings season punishes any soft spot — a small sentiment drag into the open.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a higher open: S&P 500 futures +0.28% at 7,636.25 (7:05 AM ET), Nasdaq-100 +0.24%, Dow +0.17%, Russell 2000 +0.21%; SPY +0.31% premarket at $759.47. Europe's Stoxx 600 opened -0.26% and Asian shares were mostly lower. VIX 18.22 (-0.48 vs Thursday's 18.70 close).
headlines.why_it_matters: A calmer tape after Thursday's slide, with the 10-year at 5.12% — the open now hinges on how the PPI print is digested and what Fed speakers say later today.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.1M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, ~$0.03 beat), $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M, J-W Power acquisition closed (~$860M, ~4.4M combined horsepower). WTI eased to ~$88.28 (-0.5%) after Thursday's +2.6% jump on unverified Houthi attack claims, and the IEA monthly oil report is due today — the energy tailwind stays intact, with the caveat that the oil premium rests on unconfirmed damage claims. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
